sheet-1-1.description: This part covers the lower two thirds of sheet 1 except a separately bounded block at Maple Avenue (part 2). It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, so North Green Street runs across the top of the part and East Main Street runs down its right side. Along North Green Street, between Church Street and East Main Street, stands a row of frame dwellings, with the 1st M.E. Church (heated by furnace, lit by electricity) near the middle of the block and a printing office and stores near the corner of East Main Street. A narrow open strip runs behind the lots; the interior of the block is marked vacant beyond, with the compass rose drawn in it. East Main Street is lined on its west side with stores, an auto sales room, a cement-floored building and a large brick garage with cement floor, steam heat and electric light. Further down are the Friends' Meeting House and, at the junction with Water Street and West Main Street, the Lakeside hotel (open summer only) with a boat house on the shore of Pohatcon Lake. A raceway and water pipe cross West Main Street where it bridges the outlet of the lake. A long heavy line marks the edge of what this sheet draws; the ground beyond it, lettered vacant beyond and cemetery, is left blank. The upper third of the sheet, holding the title, key map, index, key and notes on water facilities and the fire department, is outside this part's mask. House numbers along North Green Street run from about 100 to 206 and along East Main Street from 301 to 309.
notes: Population given on the title as 1500; prevailing winds W and SW.
Water works owned by the Tuckerton Water Co.: stand pipe of 50,000 gallons on a 65 ft steel tower, pumped from the lake; the fire department has a Ford pumper and a Ford chemical truck.
East Main Street / Water Street / West Main Street hand-picked at the centre of East Main Street where Water Street meets it; the detector found no junction there.
North Green Street between Church Street and East Main Street is drawn about 3 percent shorter than the modern junction spacing; sheet 2 draws it the same way.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Top third is the title, key map (500 ft to an inch), index, key and water facilities (masked out). Below: part 1 = North Green Street from Church Street to East Main Street, and East Main Street down to Water Street and Pohatcon Lake (Friends' Meeting House, Lakeside hotel); part 2 = separate block at Maple Avenue, West Main Street and Center Street, set off by a heavy L-shaped line.

sheet-1-2.description: This part is the lower left block of sheet 1, set off from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left. It shows the west end of the village around Maple Avenue, which crosses the top of the part, with West Main Street running down its left side and Center Street running down from Maple Avenue towards the bottom edge. The houses are frame dwellings, mostly of one and a half to two and a half stories, on long narrow lots, numbered 201 to 229 on West Main Street and 200 to 223 on Center Street; the blocks are numbered 32, 35, 38 and 39. Among them are an auto repairing shop with cement floor on West Main Street, several gates (G.T.) and stables or auto houses at the rear of the lots. A short Private Drive leaves West Main Street to the north-west. Block 35, north of Maple Avenue, has two dwellings and is otherwise vacant beyond. The ground west of the houses is lettered vacant beyond, and the bottom edge of the part is lettered no exposure. A dashed 6 inch water pipe runs along West Main Street and a 4 inch pipe along Maple Avenue; a hydrant stands at the corner of Maple Avenue and Center Street. Sheet 4 adjoins along Maple Avenue, where its part 2 draws West Main Street, the fork with Center Street and the triangle called Grove Place, and the two sheets repeat the junctions of Maple Avenue.
notes: Placed on one detected junction (Maple Avenue / West Main Street) with a second point derived at the atlas scale; low confidence.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Top third is the title, key map (500 ft to an inch), index, key and water facilities (masked out). Below: part 1 = North Green Street from Church Street to East Main Street, and East Main Street down to Water Street and Pohatcon Lake (Friends' Meeting House, Lakeside hotel); part 2 = separate block at Maple Avenue, West Main Street and Center Street, set off by a heavy L-shaped line.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, covers the north-west quarter of the village centre between North Green Street along the bottom and Cedar Street at the top right, with East Main Street running up the right side. Church Street and Wood Street divide it into blocks numbered 16, 26 and 27. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings, stables and auto houses on long lots; house numbers run from about 106 to 147 on North Green Street, 115 to 223 on Wood Street and 110 to 129 on Church Street. Buildings of note are the Masonic Hall on Church Street near Wood Street, a hall on East Main Street, a garage for 30 cars with cement floor, steam heat and electric light near the corner of East Main and North Green Streets, a bakery with an oven at the top of the sheet, poultry houses and a coop. A cemetery fills much of block 27 between Church Street and the left edge. The left edge is lettered vacant beyond and no exposure. Dashed water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Wood Street, Church Street, North Green Street and East Main Street, with hydrants at the corners. The top left corner of the sheet is a separately bounded inset (part 2) showing East Main Street north of Cedar Street. Marine Street and Cedar Street are lettered where they leave East Main Street on the right edge, and South Green Street and West Main Street at the bottom right corner.
notes: Church Street / North Green Street carries a residual of about 3 m on this sheet and on sheet 1; Church Street may have shifted slightly at North Green Street.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Part 1 = Church Street, Wood Street, North Green Street and the west side of East Main Street up to Cedar Street; part 2 = boxed inset top left: East Main Street north of Cedar Street (block 17).

sheet-2-2.description: This part is the boxed inset in the top left corner of sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left like the main part. It shows East Main Street north-east of Cedar Street, the continuation of the street beyond the top of the main part, with block 17 on its east side and part of block 16 on its west side. Cedar Street runs along the bottom of the inset from its junction with East Main Street. The inset holds a handful of frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories with stables and auto houses behind them, on large lots; house numbers run from 219 and 304 at Cedar Street to 504 to 514 further along East Main Street, and the far end of block 17 is lettered vacant beyond. A 4 inch water pipe runs along Cedar Street and a 4 inch and 6 inch pipe along East Main Street, with a hydrant at the junction; East Main Street is marked 60 feet wide and Cedar Street 40 feet. The numbers 2 and 3 along the edges refer to the adjoining sheets. The rest of block 17 is open ground with no buildings drawn, and the inset ends at the heavy line that separates it from the main part of the sheet below.
notes: Placed on one hand-picked junction (Cedar Street / East Main Street) with a second point derived at the atlas scale and north from the neighbouring sheets; low confidence.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Part 1 = Church Street, Wood Street, North Green Street and the west side of East Main Street up to Cedar Street; part 2 = boxed inset top left: East Main Street north of Cedar Street (block 17).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, covers the north-east part of the village centre between East Main Street on the left and the open ground beyond Clay Street on the right, from Cedar Street at the top to South Green Street at the bottom. Marine Street crosses the sheet near the top and Clay Street runs down its middle; blocks 18, 19, 24 and 25 are numbered. Most lots hold frame dwellings with stables and auto houses. Along East Main Street, near North Green Street, is the commercial core: stores, a bank, offices, the Carlton House hotel with dining room, kitchen and a grill and dance hall, a storage building and a garage for 25 cars of concrete block with cement floor, steam heat and electric light. Near Cedar Street stand the Presbyterian church and the public library. North of Marine Street, east of Clay Street, are the public school and Tuckerton High School with its auditorium and gymnasium, both heated by steam. In the middle of block 25 is the stand pipe of the water works, an iron water tank elevated 65 feet on an iron tower holding 50,000 gallons. House numbers run from about 100 to 216 on East Main Street and from about 107 to 225 on Clay Street, and the lots are long and narrow except for the school grounds. The right edge is lettered no exposure, and Wood Street and North Green Street are lettered where they leave East Main Street on the left.
notes: Stand pipe: iron water tank elevated 65 ft on an iron tower, capacity 50,000 gallons.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. East Main Street to Clay Street and beyond, between Cedar Street and North/South Green Street; Presbyterian church, public school, Tuckerton High School, Carlton House, bank, water tank.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, covers the south side of the village centre: South Green Street along the top from East Main Street, Water Street running diagonally along the north bank of Mill Creek, and West Main Street running down from the end of East Main Street along the east shore of Pohatcon Lake. Between South Green Street and Water Street (block 30) are stores, the post office and a moving picture theatre with hot-air heat and electric light near East Main Street, dwellings and, at the right, the Borough Hall in block 33. Boat houses line the creek. The largest establishment is the Tuckerton Manufacturing Co. grist mill, boat building yard and marine railways at the outlet of the lake: a grist mill and machine shop driven by a turbine from the raceway, a pump house, purifier house, hardware and wood working buildings with a gasoline engine, a lumber shed, boat building shop and marine railway. On West Main Street stand the fire department engine house with a bell tower and a concrete block garage. Much of the ground between the creek and West Main Street is marsh land, with boat houses at the water. Beaupel Place, lettered as an arbitrary name, leaves West Main Street at the bottom. Heavy lines set off two other parts of the sheet: West Main Street beyond Beaupel Place on the right (part 2) and an inset of South Green Street at the bottom left (part 3).
notes: East Main Street / Water Street / West Main Street hand-picked at the centre of East Main Street where Water Street meets it (detected point 25 ft off, excluded); Clay Street / South Green Street hand-picked, Clay Street being drawn only about 50 ft onto the sheet.
Beaupel Place (arbitrary name) has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Part 1 = South Green Street, Water Street, Mill Creek and the Tuckerton Manufacturing Co. grist mill and boat yards, West Main Street along Pohatcon Lake; part 2 = West Main Street from Beaupel Place (arbitrary name) to the Center Street fork and Maple Avenue, right of a heavy line; part 3 = boxed inset bottom left: South Green Street numbers 343 to 363, continuing sheet 5 eastwards.

sheet-4-2.description: This part is the right-hand third of sheet 4, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left. It shows West Main Street running straight down the part from Beaupel Place at the top, an arbitrary name lettered on a short street to the east, to the fork where Center Street branches off towards Maple Avenue at the bottom. The triangle between West Main Street, Center Street and Maple Avenue is block 37, lettered Grove Place. The buildings are mainly frame dwellings with stables and auto houses on deep lots; house numbers run from 111 to 167 on West Main Street and from 156 to 166 on Center Street, and the blocks are numbered 31, 32, 35 and 37. There is a factory with a gasoline engine on the west side of West Main Street, an auto paint shop, a vacant and dilapidated building, and a small store at the fork. The ground east of the houses on the right edge is lettered vacant beyond. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along West Main Street and Center Street, with hydrants on West Main Street and at the corner of Center Street and Maple Avenue. West Main Street is marked 60 feet wide, Center Street 32 feet and Beaupel Place and Maple Avenue 33 feet. Sheet 1 adjoins along Maple Avenue, and the main part of sheet 4 at Beaupel Place.
notes: Placed on two detected junctions on Maple Avenue (West Main Street and Center Street, about 190 ft apart) as a helmert fit; the upper end, about 900 ft from them, rests on their rotation; low confidence.
Beaupel Place (arbitrary name) has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Part 1 = South Green Street, Water Street, Mill Creek and the Tuckerton Manufacturing Co. grist mill and boat yards, West Main Street along Pohatcon Lake; part 2 = West Main Street from Beaupel Place (arbitrary name) to the Center Street fork and Maple Avenue, right of a heavy line; part 3 = boxed inset bottom left: South Green Street numbers 343 to 363, continuing sheet 5 eastwards.

sheet-4-3.description: This part is the boxed inset in the lower left of sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the left. It continues South Green Street eastwards beyond the right edge of sheet 5, which the number 5 on its left edge refers to, showing house numbers 343 to 363 on the north side of the street. The north side (block 23) has a row of frame dwellings of one and a half to two stories with stables or auto houses behind them on long, narrow lots. The south side (block 34) holds a gate, two small auto houses or stables and a boat building shop near the bottom of the inset, and the ground towards Pohatcon Lake is lettered vacant beyond. A 4 inch water pipe runs along South Green Street and ends at a hydrant at the right edge of the inset. No cross street is drawn in the inset, so it has no street junction of its own: its first lots repeat the last lots of sheet 5, including the house at number 341, the lot line beside it and a gate on the south side of the street. The heavy line around the inset separates it from the marsh and lake shore drawn on the main part of the sheet, which lie elsewhere on the ground.
notes: No street junction: placed from a gate and a lot line repeated on sheet 5 (carried points) at the atlas scale, with north taken from sheet 5; low confidence.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Part 1 = South Green Street, Water Street, Mill Creek and the Tuckerton Manufacturing Co. grist mill and boat yards, West Main Street along Pohatcon Lake; part 2 = West Main Street from Beaupel Place (arbitrary name) to the Center Street fork and Maple Avenue, right of a heavy line; part 3 = boxed inset bottom left: South Green Street numbers 343 to 363, continuing sheet 5 eastwards.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, covers the east end of the village between Marine Street at the top and South Green Street at the bottom, with Otis Avenue running down the middle of the sheet and Bay Avenue leaving it to the right as a short street ending in open ground. The blocks are numbered 19, 20, 22, 23, 24 and 33. Most of the sheet is open land divided into large lots, with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories and stables or auto houses along Otis Avenue (numbers 116 to 156), Marine Street (305 to 341) and South Green Street (about 230 to 341). A concrete block dwelling stands on Otis Avenue near Marine Street. A large stable or auto house stands in block 23, and the ground east of Bay Avenue is lettered ball ground. Along the bottom of the sheet, south of South Green Street, the shore of the creek is drawn with boat houses and a carpenter shop at the water. Water pipes of 4 inches run along Marine Street, Otis Avenue and South Green Street, with hydrants at Marine Street and at Otis Avenue near Bay Avenue. Otis Avenue is marked 50 feet wide and Bay Avenue 40 feet. The number 3 on the left edge refers to the adjoining sheet 3 and the number 4 at the bottom right to the inset of South Green Street on sheet 4, which continues the street eastwards.
notes: Placed from three junctions along Otis Avenue (helmert fit); the far corners rest on their rotation; medium confidence.
Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Otis Avenue between Marine Street and South Green Street, Bay Avenue stub, ball ground, boat houses on the creek.
